meta.description: Complete identity platform. Authentication, MFA, SSO, Multi-Tenancy, NHI, Authorization, Audit, Compliance, SM Crypto, SDKs — open source under AGPL.

hero.lead: 27 microservices, 1,400+ APIs, npm SDK packages, 15+ compliance frameworks — everything your AI-generated app needs for identity.

sections.title: Authentication & Registration
sections.desc: Complete user identity lifecycle — from sign-up to enterprise SSO, from basic auth to passwordless.
items: Email/password with configurable password policy (min length, complexity, history)
Password transmission encryption: plain, hash, symmetric (ECDH+AES-256-GCM), asymmetric (RSA-OAEP)
Social login: Google, GitHub, WeChat, Apple, Microsoft, DingTalk, Lark
Passwordless: Magic Link, SMS OTP, email OTP, QR code login, anonymous login
Password lifecycle: expiry, forced reset, N-previous history, per-tenant policy
Account recovery: forgot/reset password, phone/email verification, recovery codes
CAPTCHA: reCAPTCHA, Turnstile, Proof-of-Work — configurable per tenant
Password strength evaluation (zxcvbn, OWASP ASVS V6.2.8)

sections.title: Multi-Factor Authentication
sections.desc: From TOTP to phishing-resistant passkeys. Enterprise-grade MFA with risk-based adaptation.
items: TOTP (RFC 6238) — time-based one-time passwords
SMS and email OTP — via configurable provider backends
WebAuthn / FIDO2 / Passkey — platform and roaming authenticators
Push notification MFA — challenge/response with approve/deny
Adaptive MFA — risk engine: 7 signals (device/IP/geo/behavior/velocity/leak/hijack)
Backup and recovery codes — generate, verify, revoke, admin reset
Step-up authentication — re-authenticate for sensitive operations

sections.title: Enterprise SSO & Federation
sections.desc: Connect with any identity provider. Standards-compliant SAML, OIDC, OAuth implementations.
items: SAML 2.0 — SP-initiated SSO, IdP management, SLO, metadata endpoints
OpenID Connect — full provider with Discovery, UserInfo, ID Token
OAuth 2.1 — Authorization Code + PKCE (RFC 7636), refresh tokens, device code (RFC 8628)
OAuth Token Exchange (RFC 8693) — service-to-service delegation, NHI token exchange
DPoP — bind tokens to client keys, prevent replay attacks
JARM — JWT-signed authorization responses for financial-grade security
Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) — self-service OAuth client provisioning
Rich Authorization Request (RFC 9396) — structured authorization scopes
private_key_jwt — JWT-based client authentication
Social OAuth: GitHub, Google, Facebook, Discord, LinkedIn, WeChat, Apple
LDAP / Active Directory — bind authentication, user sync, group mapping
SCIM 2.0 — /scim/v2/Users and /Groups for enterprise user provisioning

sections.title: Multi-Tenancy & Organizations
sections.desc: Built for B2B SaaS. Every feature is tenant-aware by design.
items: Per-tenant data isolation — tenant_id on every query, 3-layer enforcement
Custom domains & white-label — per-tenant branding, custom login pages
Organization hierarchy — departments, org charts, delegated administration
Member management — invitations, approvals, role assignments, bulk import
Application and role management — per-tenant app CRUD, app-level roles
Tenant security policies — password policy, MFA, session timeout per tenant
Feature gates — plan-based enablement with per-tenant overrides

sections.title: Authorization & Access Control
sections.desc: From roles to attributes to relationships. Four authorization models in one platform.
items: RBAC (NIST standard) — role hierarchy, inheritance, pre-defined super_admin/admin/security_admin
ABAC — expr-lang/expr policy engine, OPA/Rego bridge, JWT/GeoIP/DeviceTrust resolvers
ReBAC — BFS relationship graph, per-tenant cache with invalidation
PIM/JIT — time-bound role activation (max 24h), approval workflow, scheduled expiry
Separation of Duties (SoD) — conflict pair detection, enforcement on all assignments
PermissionRequired middleware — fine-grained endpoint-level access control
Approval workflow — sensitive operations require multi-party approval

sections.title: NHI — Non-Human Identity
sections.desc: Identity for AI agents, robots, and IoT devices. Because AI needs its own identity.
items: AI Agent lifecycle: provisioning → active → rotating → revoked → deleted
Robot lifecycle: commissioning → active → degraded → decommissioned → deleted
IoT Device lifecycle: unpaired → active → transferring → revoked → deleted
Auth methods: client_credentials, api_key, device_code, intent_token
Delegation middleware — OnBehalfOf + Chain-ID headers for AI agent chains
Ed25519 intent token signing — signed operation scopes for delegated AI actions
Token exchange — OAuth token-exchange grant for NHI service-to-service auth

sections.title: Audit & Compliance
sections.desc: Tamper-proof audit trails with Merkle hash chain verification. Enterprise compliance frameworks.
items: Merkle hash chain audit logs — cryptographic integrity verification
GDPR DSAR automation — 7-service erasure orchestration, hash-chain audit trail
Two-level deletion — soft-delete (reversible) → anonymization (irreversible), scheduler-driven
Compliance frameworks: ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOX, PSD2, PIPL, Dengbao 2.0
Data classification — Public / Internal / Confidential / Restricted
Cross-border data transfer management
Data retention policies — configurable TTL, archive triggers
Breach notification and vendor risk assessment management
Penetration test and audit finding tracking with evidence linking

sections.title: National Cryptography (GM/T)
sections.desc: Chinese national standard cryptography. Required for government and regulated industry deployments.
items: SM2 — elliptic curve key exchange and digital signature
SM3 — cryptographic hash algorithm (256-bit)
SM4 — block cipher (CBC/PKCS7) for data encryption
Ed25519 — high-performance signature algorithm
Per-tenant crypto profile — tenant-level algorithm selection (SM vs standard)
14 integration points across the system, needs-rehash auto-detection

sections.title: Developer Platform
sections.desc: 1,400+ APIs, npm SDK packages, gRPC mesh, auto-generated TypeScript types.
items: 1,400+ RESTful API endpoints across 27 microservices, versioned and documented
gRPC service mesh — 9 microservices with gRPC interfaces
SDK: @autional/react and other npm packages published; framework adapters for Vue, Next.js and more are on the roadmap
Auto-generated TypeScript types — from OpenAPI specs (38K+ lines)
600+ webhook event types — HMAC-signed delivery across all services
Swagger/OpenAPI — interactive docs for every endpoint
TanStack Query hooks — auto-generated for all endpoints

sections.title: Infrastructure & Integrations
sections.desc: Multi-provider, cloud-native. Run anywhere — your infrastructure, your control.
items: PostgreSQL + PgBouncer, MongoDB, Redis, RabbitMQ, Kafka, ZooKeeper

pricing.title: Simple, Transparent Pricing
pricing.lead: Self-hosted open source is available today; cloud hosting is on the roadmap (coming soon). The tiers below are planned cloud offerings — no surprise bills, no vendor lock-in.

faqs.q: Can I self-host Autional for free?
faqs.a: Yes. Autional's core is AGPL open source. You can self-host the entire 27-service stack using Docker — no license fee, no MAU limits. Cloud hosting is on the roadmap (coming soon).
A Monthly Active User is a unique user who authenticates within a calendar month. If a user signs in once during the month, they count as 1 MAU. Idle users do not count.

faqs.q: Can I upgrade from Free to Pro without migrating?
faqs.a: Yes. Upgrading unlocks higher limits and additional features instantly. No data migration, no code changes, no downtime.

faqs.q: Do you offer discounts for open-source projects?
faqs.a: Once cloud launches, we plan to offer special pricing for open-source projects and non-profit organizations. Contact us for details.

faqs.q: What payment methods do you accept?
faqs.a: Once cloud launches, we'll support all major credit cards via Stripe. For Enterprise plans, we also plan to support wire transfers and annual invoicing.

trust.title: Trust & Compliance
trust.lead: Autional is built with security and compliance as core design principles — not afterthoughts.

cards.title: Data Encryption
cards.desc: All sensitive fields encrypted with AES-256-GCM at rest. Key rotation supported. SM4-GCM for Chinese national standard compliance.

cards.title: Password Security
cards.desc: argon2id hashing with per-tenant pepper. Password transmission supports ECDH symmetric and RSA asymmetric encryption.

cards.title: Audit Trail
cards.desc: Immutable Merkle hash chain audit logs. Every authentication event is cryptographically linked and verifiable.

cards.title: MFA & Access Control
cards.desc: TOTP, WebAuthn/FIDO2, SMS, email, push MFA. RBAC + ABAC + ReBAC + PIM authorization models.

cards.title: Compliance Frameworks
cards.desc: Built-in data models and tooling for: ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOX, GDPR, PSD2, PIPL, Dengbao 2.0.

cards.title: Key Management
cards.desc: Centralized secret-service for encryption keys, JWT signing keys, and API keys — sensitive credentials never live in business code.

cards.title: Architecture
cards.desc: 27 independently deployable microservices. PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, RabbitMQ. gRPC service mesh with OpenTelemetry tracing.

cards.title: Vulnerability Management
cards.desc: Regular dependency scanning, a public vulnerability disclosure channel, and security audit finding tracking built into the compliance service.

trust.disclaimer: The technical capabilities described above represent Autional's platform design goals and built-in tooling. Compliance certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, etc.) are the responsibility of the deploying organization. Autional provides the technical foundation — achieving certification requires organization-specific controls, audits, and policies.

ai.heroTitle: Turn your app into a multi-user product
ai.heroLead: Paste one prompt into your AI coding agent. It fetches the onboarding skill — a guided procedure for adding Autional login, accounts, and sessions to your existing project. Falls back to an own-CDN mirror if the site is unreachable.
ai.agentNote: Works in Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, or any agent with web access.
ai.promptPrimary:
Fetch {{url}} and follow it to add Autional login to this project. If unreachable, use:
{{fallback}}
ai.promptSecondarySummary: Prefer Chinese? Use this prompt instead
ai.step2Desc: Run it in the project you want to upgrade. The agent reads the skill and works through it phase by phase, confirming with you at each gate.
ai.step3Desc: The agent inspects your app first, then proposes the plan — you approve before anything is changed. Everything lands on a separate git branch.

phases.title: Safety net first
phases.desc: Git branch, toolkit check, risk disclosure — every change is reversible.

phases.title: Inspect your app
phases.desc: Framework, existing auth, conflicts, and what the integration will change.

phases.title: Design the policy
phases.desc: Tenant naming, compliance-driven password policy, login methods.

phases.title: Provision identity
phases.desc: Tenant + application created in the developer portal; credentials handled once.

phases.title: Wire it in
phases.desc: Provider, login UI, external-id mapping, user center — real code, then verify the build.

phases.title: Test & verify
phases.desc: Unit tests plus an 8-step end-to-end flow: register → login → profile → refresh → logout → revoked.

phases.title: Hand over
phases.desc: Change inventory, test accounts, and what to check in the portals.
